rotated_exact_queries.result: The reviewed first page contains source or documentation, not emitted transfer/use records. Page two is not retained as a cursor; narrower content-addressed variants replace it.

aggregate.method: GitHub default-branch code search. Rows are locators until the original file, pinned repository context and commit history are read.
aggregate.transient_errors: Search rate limits were retried without widening scope.

selected_repository.selected_reason: Two independent rotations reached an original repository containing explicit inter-agent contract requests plus a content-specific fix, integration and later verification chain.

work_orders.finding: Human-facing instructions define one of four concurrent coding roles and permit coordination only through the repository contract-request file.
Human-facing instructions assign the purchasing lane inside the same four-agent plan.
Human-facing instructions assign a third bounded implementation lane.
Human-facing instructions assign frontend, demonstration and evaluation work.

build_spec.finding: The project calls this the single source of truth for four concurrent coding agents and labels behavior as verified, assumed or simulated.

coordination_ledger.finding: The public file records requests and statuses among the four assigned roles, repeatedly reserves decisions and publication to a human lead, and contains the selected purchasing dependency.

runbook.finding: The demo runbook identifies simulated and mock fallbacks and does not establish a live autonomous exchange outside the project.

product_readme.finding: The product description retains user opt-in and owner approvals and labels the bulk-deal demonstration as simulated.

dependency_chain.finding: The platform lane records two concrete failures in the purchasing lane: a missing required pool-account reference and a recipient lookup that searched the wrong post-match intent set. It asks the purchasing lane to review rather than silently taking ownership of that lane.
The purchasing lane selects a seeded pool account instead of a null reference and resolves the exact recipient member's intent instead of searching only shared intents.
dependency_chain.chronology_limit: The author timestamp predates the request while the committer timestamp follows it. Exact semantic correspondence and later integration support dependency, but this is not independent runtime telemetry.

dependency_chain.finding: The platform lane integrates the purchasing corrections and adds the shared checks, establishing downstream use of the foreign-lane result.
The merge message explicitly describes authorized publication and preservation of both agents' notes.
A third human-published lane records that main is green after the purchasing integration.

dependency_assessment.provider_or_model_attribution: Commit co-author trailers are project-authored metadata, not independent provider attestations or execution provenance.

authorization_and_alternatives.designed_team: Strongly supported by four explicit work orders, one shared build specification and a designated repository coordination file.
authorization_and_alternatives.human_direction: Strongly supported by repeated human-lead decisions, branch policy and an explicitly authorized publication merge.
authorization_and_alternatives.single_operator_automation: Multiple human publishing accounts make a literal one-account explanation incomplete, but do not establish separate autonomous operators or a boundary crossing.
authorization_and_alternatives.human_requested_outreach: No foreign outreach or unassigned recipient is needed to explain the chain.
authorization_and_alternatives.repeated_tests_or_retries: The selected chain is substantive development and verification, not inferred from duplicate text or retry volume.
authorization_and_alternatives.shared_state_fault: The identified failures are ordinary integration defects corrected inside the planned workflow.
authorization_and_alternatives.observer_contamination: Self-index rows were separated before selection; the dependency comes from pinned origin records and Git history.

prior_reporting_check.result: No prior coordination report located in this exact checked scope as of 2026-10-25. The exact work-order phrase resolves only to the four origin files; the exact request label resolves only to the origin coordination ledger. Search absence does not establish global novelty and is not used to promote this authorized workflow.

classification.reason: The sender-to-recipient dependency is concrete, but every transfer stays inside an explicitly assigned four-agent hackathon workflow. Human leads define roles, retain branch and publication authority, and approve the integration. No primary evidence shows cooperation beyond an operator-defined boundary.

missing_evidence_to_advance: Primary evidence that an agent-originated transfer escaped the assigned repository, task or human-lead authorization.
Independently attributable runtime or session provenance rather than project-authored role names or commit trailers.
A recipient action outside the designed work order and contract-request workflow.
An owner, operator or policy record showing that the cooperation itself violated an authorization boundary.

next_cursors.rationale: Refines the rejected broad parent/child selector toward content-addressed emitted use.
Requires both lineage and a recipient-side action.
Looks for an exact review-to-implementation adoption edge.
Looks for separately committed sender and recipient records.

next_cursors.condition: Revisit only if a public later record shows an unassigned recipient, independently attributable runtime or cooperation outside the human-approved project workflow.

safeguards.sanitization: Original public record links, timestamps and hashes are retained. Raw task/session identifiers, payload bodies, credentials, tokens, sink topics, personal addresses and private paths are omitted.
